articles.title: Create a job from scratch
articles.locator: Before you begin; Create a new job
articles.summary: Creating a basic job and associating it with a client.
facts: Every job must be associated with a client; the client may already exist or be added during job creation.
One documented starting point is the Dashboard quick-add menu, using its create-new-job option.
Complete the job information, client, template if applicable, and scheduling details on the new-job form.
Saving creates the basic job and opens its detail screen for further information.
conditions: This is navigation guidance, not authority to create or modify a customer's records.
Do not infer accounting configuration or permissions from these selected facts.

articles.title: About timesheets
articles.locator: Entering time and viewing timesheets; Frequently Asked Questions
articles.summary: Where people enter their own time and the conditions for weekly entry.
facts: Staff can enter their own time through the Dashboard quick-add time-entry option or through their personal timesheets screen.
Weekly time entry requires the organisation's Weekly Timesheet Entry setting to be enabled.
The weekly timesheet view does not save automatically; its save control must be used.
Submitting a week's timesheet locks it against further entries.
conditions: Do not assume an organisation setting or permission is already enabled.
The absence of autosave does not establish the cause of a reported error after saving.

articles.title: About quick time entry
articles.locator: Introduction; Draft quick time entries; Using the timer
articles.summary: Quick time recording, incomplete drafts, access limits and submitted records.
facts: The menu-bar timer opens quick time entry to record work as it happens or manage entries.
If the required job is not visible because of permissions, contact the system administrator or support.
A submitted timesheet is locked: entries can be viewed but not changed in that state.
A quick-time entry remains a draft until the required time, client, job and task details are complete.
conditions: Do not offer a permission bypass or assume the requester may unlock a timesheet.
The selected facts do not include an approved unlock procedure.
